title: Grateful Dead Live at San Jose Civic Auditorium on 1972-08-20
lineage: Master cassettes played back on Nakamichi Dragon > Digital Audio Labs Card Deluxe soundcard (96Mhz/24 bit)> HD > Adobe Audition; L3 Multimaximizer>Waves Z-Noise; Dithered and downsampled to 44.1 MHz / 16 bit; Flac Encoded
source: Sony TC-124 with Sony Stereo Mic (Pacific Stereo Cassettes)

ai_review.summary: Muddy, slightly noisy tape that improves midway – the highlight is a solid The Other One while Bertha suffers from poor sound.
ai_review.review: The recording is uneven; early tracks are muddy, a half‑step fast, and even contain noise and a cut at the end of Truckin', making Bertha almost unlistenable. However, the second disc picks up with a strong performance of The Other One (though Mickey Hart’s “ravenous tiger” isn’t fully captured). Overall sentiment is mixed, reflecting both the show’s musical moments and the sub‑par audio quality.

ai_rating.rationale: One detailed review points to significant recording flaws but praises The Other One; a brief five‑star review is enthusiastic but lacks specifics, yielding an overall moderate rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Sound described as slightly muddy, half‑step fast, with weird noise and a cut at the end of Truckin'. Bertha is nearly unlistenable; overall tape improves later in the set.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early part of the show suffers from audio issues, while the second disc (starting with Bird Song) feels stronger and more cohesive.

band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Hart’s ‘ravenous tiger’ doesn’t quite come through in the mix.
